beats.heading: Behind the upload
beats.narration_text: This is my Week Eight Humanitarians AI progress report, covering October twenty sixth through November first. I supported Sanjana's YouTube workflow by preparing titles and descriptions for submissions. My focus was publication preparation, not technical source code review or changes to anyone's project. Liam, narrating for Deepa.

beats.heading: Four contributors. Fourteen videos.
beats.narration_text: My work covered fourteen submissions from four contributors. Tanmay contributed four videos, Anjana four, Mohammed four, and Uday two. These are the counts in my work account. Keeping the contributor and submission count visible helped define the scope of this report. Four plus four plus four plus two gives fourteen videos, each needing clear publishing information.

beats.heading: Start with the submitted information
beats.narration_text: I used the submitted topics and filenames to understand what each video was about before preparing its metadata. The goal was to represent the actual submission, not make a more impressive claim than the material supported. This report does not attach unverified individual titles to contributors. It focuses on the preparation work I can describe: identifying the subject, organizing the wording, and keeping the description relevant to the submission.
on_screen_text: Metadata is not a code review.

beats.heading: A title should set the right expectation
beats.narration_text: For the titles, I focused on clear subject identification and concise, readable wording. A viewer should understand what the video covers before pressing play. I worked to keep titles aligned with the submitted content rather than imply results or achievements that were not established. The important question was simple: does this wording accurately describe this video? A strong title can be informative without making exaggerated promises.

beats.heading: Descriptions add useful context
beats.narration_text: I also prepared descriptions that summarized the subject, educational purpose, and key concepts of each submission. A description gives viewers more context than a title alone. My role was to communicate the topic clearly and consistently. It was not to certify the project's implementation or independently verify its technical results. Keeping that boundary clear matters, because publishing copy should not accidentally sound like an approval or a technical audit.

beats.heading: Preparation is not publication
beats.narration_text: The prepared videos and metadata were sent for Sanjana's review. Prepared, submitted for approval, approved, and published are different stages. This report records preparation and submission for approval. It does not claim that the fourteen videos were approved or publicly published. Maintaining those distinctions makes the status easier to understand and prevents a completed description from being mistaken for a completed publishing decision.

beats.heading: What I learned
beats.narration_text: Week Eight's result was titles and descriptions prepared for fourteen videos from four contributors, with submissions sent for approval. I learned the value of consistent metadata and clear contributor coordination. Good publishing support helps the next reviewer understand the content and its status. It does not replace that review. Humanitarians AI.
